title: docs(adr): ADR-0112 amendment — `error.code` is closed at every door, `declaredCode` is the open channel (#9106)
body:
Fixes #9106

⚠️ **This PR carries the closing keyword, and the implementation PR (#9234) deliberately does not** — PM ruling, superseding the original dispatch instruction. The ruling on #9106 names the ADR prose as the deliverable that matters most, so the card must not auto-close when the code lands while this sits unmerged behind a human-approval gate. #9234 says `Part of #9106`; #9106 closes when **this** lands.

⛔ **Maintainer-merged, per Prime Directive #14.** Its diff touches `docs/adr/**`, so no AI seat merges it, queues it, or arms auto-merge on it — reviewed, approved and fully green does not change that. Left as a draft. ⚠️ Note the consequence of the keyword swap: #9106 now stays open until a human merges this, which is the intended behaviour, not an oversight.

## Why this is a deliverable and not documentation debt

The ruling on #9106 made the ADR text a deliverable in its own right, and the card's own analysis says why it matters more than the code: an agent reading ADR-0112 today concludes `error.code` is closed and may write a consumer that switches exhaustively on it — **wrong at exactly one door, and wrong in a way no gate reports.** Fixing the code without fixing the prose leaves the misleading half in place.

## What the amendment records

Added on D4 (the ruling that closed the *schema*, which is the one this qualifies):

- **`error.code` is closed at every door.** A thrown code outside `StandardErrorCode` union the serving side's ledger is demoted; `code` carries the member the status derives.
- **`declaredCode` is the open, author-authored channel** — the boundary named explicitly, with **presence means demotion** fixed as its semantics (absent when the producer's code IS a member, absent when it declared none).
- **#7867's sandbox passthrough is preserved, not retired** — and narrowing the sandbox boundary is recorded as the rejected alternative, with the reason.
- **Where it is pinned** — the resolver, the three dispatcher exits, and the three test files, so the decision is findable from the code and vice versa.
- **⛔ `DUPLICATE` is deliberately not registered**, and why registering one tenant spelling would close nothing.
- **Scope** — the doors served by `resolveThrownHttpError`. `packages/rest`'s flat dialect puts `code` at the body's top level, is out of scope, and is filed as #9232.

Plus one Consequences bullet: the wire change for author-thrown codes, and the fact that the ruling's binding precondition was measured empty before landing, by two independent search shapes.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **A stale citation is corrected in passing.** #9098's prose points at **#7035** as the open envelope-position finding; #7035 is no longer open (landed via PR #7293, three `/meta` 501 handlers). The amendment names #9232 instead.
- **The scope paragraph is deliberately descriptive, not a carve-out.** It says where the amendment's rule was measured to hold and points at #9232 for the flat `sendThrownError` door; it does **not** narrow the ruling's own words. Whether "every door" should formally exclude that door is the maintainer's call, recorded on #9232.
- `pnpm check:adr-anchors` green — all 25907 citations across the tree still resolve, and every anchored file still references its governing ADR.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` green; the file was also scanned directly for control bytes.
- Docs-only, publishes nothing — `skip-changeset` applied (label list read back after the bots settled: `documentation`, `size/s`, `skip-changeset`).
